title: Random forest on fMRI network variability classifies major depressive disorder
summary: A random forest model combining temporal and spatial variability features of dynamic brain networks distinguished patients with major depressive disorder from healthy controls, with AUC 0.946 in a discovery cohort (119 patients, 106 controls) and 0.834 in an external Rest-meta-MDD cohort (126 patients, 124 controls). A linear model on the same features predicted depression severity (r=0.640) and anxiety (r=0.616). Validation performance was lower than discovery.
ai_technology: Random forest on integrated temporal and spatial fMRI variability features

evidence.tested: Discovery and external validation cohorts from the Rest-meta-MDD consortium.
evidence.unknown: Modest validation AUC; clinical utility not shown; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest classification and linear regression on fMRI features.
